messages:
ana: quick sync — we noticed background job auth failures: `ingest-cleanup` using a service API key is blocked from accessing project-scoped resources.
vikram: yep, root cause is missing project claim on svc tokens. Recent RBAC changes started enforcing `project:<id>` claims for project resources.
maria: does the edge proxy try to infer project from svc metadata today?
ana: no, proxy treats non-project tokens as org-level service actors. theres no synthesis.
vikram: we sketched three paths: (A) broaden service permissions (fast, too permissive). (B) proxy synthesizes project claim from a mapping table (pragmatic short-term, but implicit elevation risk). (C) require jobs to use ephemeral project-scoped tokens minted by a broker (ideal long-term).
josh: (C) is the right security posture. (B) could be a temporary band-aid if well-audited.
ana: infra proposal: add a controlled mapping in AuthN: service_id -> allowed project ids. AuthN can assert a project claim when the svc token is used by a verified internal worker queue and when the org has opted in. precedence: explicit project token > asserted-mapping claim > plain svc token.
maria: please gate assertion per-org via a feature flag. we must avoid implicit claims across customers.
vikram: Agreed — feature-flag per org plus audit log entries. Also emit a header `X-Auth-Decision: mapped-project` for observability.
dev-bot: suggested PR checklist:
- DB migration: table `service_project_mappings`
- Admin API: POST /admin/v1/mappings, GET /admin/v1/mappings/:svc_id
- Feature flag: `auth.assert_mapped_projects` per-org
- Audit log: record {actor, svc_id, mapped_project_id, asserted_by, trace_id}
josh: smoke test we can run after mapping creation:
```
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer svc-abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/projects/proj-123/resources
# expect 200 and header: X-Auth-Decision: mapped-project
```
nana: long-term RFC: "service-auth-unification" — migrate all system jobs to short-lived project-scoped tokens via workload identity (broker). estimate ~3 months. migration path: run dual-accept mode (broker tokens + mapped assertions) for ~6 weeks, then require broker tokens.
maria: I'll mock the mapping schema + admin UI. sketch mapping record:
```
svc_id: svc-ingest-01
allowed_projects: [proj-123, proj-456]
owner: team-data-platform
reason: ingest jobs for datasets X,Y
expires_at: null
```
vikram: add TTL and rotation guidance. mappings should be reviewed/rotated every 30 days.
sre-bot: alert rule suggestion: fire if mapped-project decisions have >1% authorization failures in last hour (possible stale mapping).
josh: add an acceptance test simulating project removal to ensure requests fail when mapping revoked.
nana: action items: @maria owns mapping API + UI, @vikram owns auth service change + trace header, @ana drafts RFC and migration plan, @josh adds CI tests/canary. I'll open tickets and a tiny PR tomorrow for DB migration + feature flag. :thumbsup:
vikram: I'll stand up a canary cluster, load a small backlog to validate the path, and post metrics to #eng-sre.
maria: ack, starting design now.
nana: no objections, proceed — low-risk, auditable, buys time for broker migration. thanks everyone.
